A "not published" column stays in the tables, empty, with a status field next to it. That way the join is already in place on the day someone publishes the number, and nobody mistakes a blank for a zero.

The City's budget rows

I read the City's two current documents from the public pages of its People's Budget Portal: the enacted 2026 budget ({{ab_rows}} rows, {{ab_total}}) and the proposed 2027 Annual Investment Program ({{aip_rows}} rows, {{aip_total}}). (The 2026 overview page's headline is ₱2.12 billion; the difference is ₱457.66 million of special purpose appropriations, which that page states but the Browse page doesn't list.) The Browse page of each carries every published row with its AIP reference code, office, and PS/MOOE/CO split. For the rows of eight offices (education, early childhood, nutrition, child welfare, the library, the science centre and the city college), I also read each row's own page, which lists its funds.

(I help build that portal through Stride Technologies, which is exactly why I kept to the pages any resident's browser receives. The portal's bulk open-data API is switched off for both years by the City's choice, so I didn't use it, and nothing here comes from the admin side.)

Each row then gets a domain from a short list of rules. The first rule that matches wins, and its ID is kept on the row as tag_rule:

{{rules_rows}}
RuleOfficesRow name matchesDomain

The explorer's default total counts {{default_domains}}. In the 2027 AIP that comes to {{aip_edu}} across {{aip_edu_lines}} rows, and in the enacted 2026 budget to {{ab_edu}} across {{ab_edu_lines}} rows. Those two aren't comparable as a trend: the 2027 figure includes the SEF row and the 2026 one can't (see below).

{{lines_with_place}} of {{lines_total}} of those rows name a school or a barangay. Every one is city-wide, so place_level is "city" throughout and each row is listed on the checks page as unplaced.

The SEF

In the 2027 AIP, the Special Education Fund appears as a single row: "Management of the Special Education Fund and Secretariat Support to the Naga City School Board", {{aip_sef}}, all of it MOOE, funded by the SEF. That one row is {{aip_sef_share}} of the education and early-childhood total, and it names no school.

The enacted 2026 rows on the portal carry no fund field at all, and none of them is the SEF. The SEF has its own budget, prepared with the Local School Board, and the portal doesn't carry it. So for 2026 I can't put a peso figure on the SEF from public data.

DepEd's own files fill in part of the picture from the school side. In SY 2023-24, Naga's public schools reported {{staff_sef}} staff paid from the City SEF ({{teachers_sef}} of them teachers, the rest mostly learning support aides and administrative staff) at {{schools_sef}} schools, plus {{staff_lgu}} paid from other LGU funds, and {{ict_items}} ICT items (mostly TVs and printers) at {{schools_ict}} schools bought with LGU or SEF money. The 2027 SEF row has no PS at all, while the schools report SEF-paid staff. Those are different years and possibly different accounting, so I'd bring it to the City School Board as a question.

DepEd's school data

DepEd publishes school-level files under Project Bukas on its machine-ready files page. I take every school whose division is "Naga City": {{schools_all}} in SY 2025-26, of which {{schools_public}} are public, {{schools_private}} private and one a state college. The public schools sit in {{districts}} school districts and enrol {{learners_public}} learners ({{kinder_public}} in kindergarten).

From the SY 2023-24 files I take instructional classrooms, buildings needing major repair (or marked for condemnation or demolition), makeshift rooms, staff by funding source, and ICT equipment by funding source. {{public_in_2023}} of the {{schools_public}} public schools appear in those files; the {{schools_missing_2023}} schools that don't (new schools, or new IDs) keep blanks and are listed as gaps.

DepEd's CSVs mix two text encodings, sometimes within one file, so school names like "Concepcion Pequeña" arrive garbled. The pipeline repairs each cell's encoding and leaves the numbers alone.

Reading results

DepEd's own machine-ready CRLA file has {{crla_rows}} schools, all from {{crla_regions}}, so it has none of Naga's (ELLNA and NAT are the same). The school-level results are in EDCOM 2's Early Childhood Dashboard instead, which is a public Tableau workbook whose author allows downloads. Its CRLA table is keyed by DepEd school ID and labelled "{{crla_note}}". {{crla_public}} of Naga's {{public_es}} public elementary schools are in it. The one that isn't is {{crla_missing_es}}, and the high schools don't take CRLA at all, since it covers Grades 1 to 3.

Across those schools, {{crla_low}} of {{crla_assessed}} learners ({{crla_low_share}}) read at the Low Emerging level, and {{crla_struggling_share}} are struggling readers (Low or High Emerging, the dashboard's own measure). By district the share runs from {{crla_dist_min}} to {{crla_dist_max}}, and the highest single school is {{crla_school_max}}.

The Evidence for Education Coalition cites Naga's City School Board using Project Bukas data to realign the SEF towards remediation and furniture, after which the share of low emerging readers fell from 40% to 4%. That was Naga's own work, done by hand. The end-of-year figure here ({{crla_low_share}}) is in line with it, though I can't rebuild the 40% starting point from public data.

ECCD indicators

The same workbook has two early-childhood tables. Its 2025 Operation Timbang Plus report has one row for the City of Naga: {{opt_measured}} children under five measured (of an estimated {{opt_est}}), of whom {{opt_stsst}} ({{opt_share}}) were stunted or severely stunted. On the dashboard's own stunting measure, which EDCOM 2 describes as children aged 0 to 2, it's {{opt_e2_st}} of {{opt_e2_n}} ({{opt_e2_share}}). There's no barangay breakdown, so that column in barangays.csv stays empty with a status of "city level only".

For child development centres, the workbook has a list of barangays without one (it doesn't say where the list comes from). None of Naga's {{barangays}} barangays is on it. That gives a yes or no per barangay; how many centres each one has isn't published.

edcom2.gov.ph sits behind a bot check, which I cleared by hand once to see what the page embeds. The pipeline reads the workbook straight from public.tableau.com, where there's no check, and it stops if the author ever turns data access off. Only Naga's rows are kept.

Places

Barangays come from PSA's 2026 PSGC (as parsed by bendlikeabamboo/barangay, tag {{psgc_tag}}): Naga has {{barangays}}. Each school's barangay name from DepEd is matched to a PSGC code after folding case and accents. {{matched}} of {{schools_all}} schools match. Two names needed a hand match ({{alias_list}}), which affects {{alias_schools}} schools; each is listed on the checks page so the match can be checked. {{barangays_with_school}} of the {{barangays}} barangays have a public school.

Boundaries are faeldon's philippines-json-maps {{geo_tag}}, medium resolution. The map is drawn as plain SVG, with no tile server, so the site makes no third-party requests at all.

Checks and gaps

For each budget document, the rows must add up to the total the page itself states, and each row's PS, MOOE, FE and CO must add up to its total. {{checks_match}} of {{checks}} checks pass. Everything that couldn't be joined, or has no public source, is a row in gaps.csv ({{gaps_total}} rows). The checks page lists them all.

What to keep in mind

An appropriation is permission to spend. What was actually paid out sits in the City's accountability reports, which aren't here. The years don't line up either: the budget is FY 2026 and 2027, enrollment is SY 2025-26, and staff, ICT and facilities are SY 2023-24. DepEd's figures are what schools reported through its information systems, as published. DepEd's ICT files lump "LGU or SEF" together, so those items can't be split by fund.

Rerun it
uv run python -m pipeline.fetch     # DepEd files, PSGC, boundaries, the City's portal pages
uv run python -m pipeline.build     # tables, checks, gaps, API, OpenAPI, data package
uv run python -m pipeline.site      # this page and the proposal
uv run python -m pipeline.test_pipeline
